markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Diagnosis favors specific recurring interests over broad associations. This motivates pooling supported by repeated textual themes. (2) Older purchases may represent completed needs. Recency should therefore moderate recurrence evidence without claiming to identify ownership or satisfaction. (3) Existing probes measure embedding alignment and sampled training margins. They cannot establish semantic relevance or validation improvement.

**Related work.** (1) HyperHawkes separates repeated intent dynamics from short-term adaptation. This motivates combining recurrence support with recency, without assuming its results transfer here. (2) Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning warns that history perturbations can change meaning. Matched pooling and shuffled-text controls can help distinguish semantic contributions from generic pooling effects. (3) On Sampled Metrics shows that sampled evaluation can misrepresent full-ranking comparisons. Selection must retain the pinned benchmark, with full-catalog recommendations serving separate diagnostics.

### Directions and framework

Three directions follow: conservative recurrence modeling, mechanism-focused controls, and evaluation that separates predictive gains from behavioral interpretation.

| Component | Evidence available | Proposed role | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Ordered interactions | Sequential preference | Specific recurring themes |
| Text recurrence | Titles/descriptions | Support historical pooling | Similarity does not establish demand |
| Recency | Interaction order | Attenuate older evidence | Seasonal intent remains uncertain |
| Controls | Matched histories and candidates | Test incremental benefit | Latent motives remain unobserved |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality / future potential / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Bounded recurrence residual — 5/7/4.** Originality: targeted combination, but familiar ingredients. Potential: interpretable extension, but metadata coverage may limit benefit. Difficulty: small model change, but causal pooling and predictor parity require care. Inspired by HyperHawkes.
2. **Recency-only residual — 2/5/2.** Originality: useful comparator, but standard pooling. Potential: inexpensive improvement, but cannot distinguish recurring themes. Difficulty: straightforward implementation, but padding and normalization still matter.
3. **Text-supported redundancy penalty — 5/5/5.** Originality: targets completed-demand hypotheses, but resembles similarity penalties. Potential: may reduce substitutes, but can suppress desirable entertainment continuity. Difficulty: lexical evidence is available, but reliable capability judgments are difficult. Motivated by Learning to Forget.

### Selected idea

At 10% progress, prioritize the bounded recurrence residual. Fit TF–IDF using training-item titles/descriptions only. At each causal position, give historical items recurrence support from positive similarity to distinct items at separated earlier positions; multiply support by recency decay. Pool their learned ID embeddings, normalize its magnitude, and add it to SASRec through a bounded, zero-initialized scalar gate. Missing support yields zero residual.

Compare against branch-free, mean-pooling, recency-pooling, and frequency-bin shuffled-text variants within the shared budget. Use identical validation users and candidates; report macro HR@10 and paired user-bootstrap differences. Inference removal measures dependence; separately trained controls assess incremental benefit. Preserve all four dataset routes, seeds, splits, predictor serialization, and diagnosis interfaces. No performance gain or latent-user explanation is established before evaluation.

idea.description: Add a causal, bounded recurring-interest pooling residual to each SASRec representation. Training-only TF–IDF similarities identify historical items supported by another distinct, temporally separated item; recency attenuates their weights. Retain the branch during prediction.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis suggests that specific repeated interests and recent activity provide more useful evidence than broad historical associations. A zero-initialized residual permits a conservative extension of SASRec while making its incremental contribution testable. Text similarity remains a proxy, not evidence of compatibility, current need, or latent traits.
idea.implementation_notes: Fit a separate TF–IDF vocabulary per dataset using only titles/descriptions of items observed in training interactions; unavailable text maps to zero. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. For each sequence prefix, exclude padding and require distinct item IDs with an order gap of at least three positions for recurrence evidence. Use fixed sparse text features and batched similarity calculations or cached item-pair similarities; do not materialize a dense catalog similarity matrix. Normalize pooled ID embeddings to the detached norm of the corresponding SASRec feature, using epsilon safeguards. Set the residual coefficient to 0.25*tanh(g), with trainable g initialized to zero. Cache and serialize all vocabulary, text features, hyperparameters, and model parameters beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer and compatibility view so log2feats returns augmented features and predict_score uses the trained scoring head. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; run probes on the actual trained module with mode restoration. Retain existing embedding and margin probes, and optionally add gate magnitude and supported-position fraction with explicit definitions. Missing metadata or insufficient support must yield finite zero residuals. Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Charge all training and controls to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; do not assume every proposed control can be completed.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset independently:
  fit fixed normalized TF-IDF vectors x on training-item titles/descriptions
  initialize SASRec and scalar g = 0
  for each training batch:
    h = SASRec(sequence)  # causal B x L x D
    for each nonpadding position t:
      for each historical position i <= t:
        J = {j <= t: abs(i-j) >= 3, item[j] != item[i], item[j] != 0}
        support[i] = max({max(0, dot(x[item[i]], x[item[j]])): j in J}, default=0)
        weight[i] = support[i] * exp(-(t-i)/tau)
      if sum(weight) > 0:
        pool = sum_i(weight[i] * item_embedding[item[i]]) / sum(weight)
        residual = pool / max(norm(pool), epsilon) * stop_gradient(norm(h[t]))
      else:
        residual = 0
      feature[t] = h[t] + 0.25 * tanh(g) * residual
    optimize the baseline next-item objective using feature
  serialize model and fixed text state; write matching predictor
Evaluate trained variants on identical pinned validation candidates.
Compare macro HR@10 and bootstrap paired user hit differences within each category.
Use inference ablation only to measure dependence; use retrained controls to assess incremental benefit.

originality.positive: Combines explicit recurrence evidence, recency weighting, and conservative residual initialization into a narrowly testable SASRec extension.
originality.negative: Semantic similarity, historical pooling, and gated residuals are established components; novelty lies primarily in their combination and controls.

future_potential.positive: Provides a tractable foundation for examining when repeated semantic evidence improves sequential prediction across heterogeneous domains.
future_potential.negative: Lexical overlap can encode popularity or broad association, and validation gains would not establish the proposed behavioral interpretation.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no pretrained weights and preserves the baseline scoring objective and item vocabulary.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal similarities, sparse metadata handling, and exact training–prediction parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: HyperHawkes (2025)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes modeling repeated intent dynamics alongside short-term adaptation, motivating separate recurrence and recency signals.
limitations: Does not establish that TF–IDF pooling captures recurring interests or improves this four-dataset benchmark.

related_work.title: Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning (2025)
contributions: Highlights that random history augmentation can produce semantically inconsistent sequences.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed matched-control protocol; perturbation effects can still reflect distribution shift.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield comparisons inconsistent with full-ranking evaluation.
limitations: Does not determine the magnitude of sampling effects under this pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: Learning to Forget (2026 preprint)
contributions: The supplied summary motivates treating some purchases as possible intent completion.
limitations: Interaction histories and text alone cannot verify completion, ownership, or whether similar unseen items are redundant.

related_work.title: Learning to Counterfactually Explain Recommendations
contributions: Motivates distinguishing inference-time history-removal effects from counterfactual questions requiring retraining.
limitations: Inference ablations alone cannot establish incremental training benefit or users’ latent motives.
